title: Canonical ordinary quotient and finite K-flat reduction computation
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $W$. Use the actual completed and finite coefficient module categories and scalar restrictions [def-sf-scalar-reduction-categories-restriction], the positive quotient coefficients [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], finite derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and its quotient projections [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Define coefficientOrdinaryQuotient for $n\le m$ as the canonical ordinary natural map from extension to $B_m$ into restriction of extension to $B_n$, the mate of the ordinary scalar-extension unit under successive scalar restrictions; its pure-tensor formula is $b\otimes x\mapsto q_{m,n}(b)\otimes x$. For a K-flat completed-module complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], define coefficientFiniteReductionModel at level $n$ to be the canonical isomorphism from derived finite extension of $QP$ to $Q(P\otimes B_n)$: compose the localization/homotopy identification, the universal derived scalar-extension counit on $P$ (invertible on K-flat complexes by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]), and the localization identification back. These specify existing canonical maps, not new existence or compatibility claims. Scheme and coefficient universes are independent.
